Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: Social 2.1.8 Class Leadership By the end of the sub-strand, the  Learners to li
Topic 2.1.9: The school

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on The school. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify members of the (Head teacher, teachers, non-teaching 2. What is the importance school community staff and learners) of the school

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: THE SCHOOL
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
The school helps you succeed in ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: THE SCHOOL
Study The school like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify members of the (Head teacher, teachers, non-teaching 2. What is the importance school community staff and learners) of the school

What this means
In this part you learn to identify members of the (Head teacher, teachers, non-teaching 2. What is the importance school community staff and learners) of the school. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify members of the (Head teacher, teachers, non-teaching 2. What is the importance school community staff and learners) of the school.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “The school” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify members of the (Head teacher, teachers, non-teaching 2. What is the importance school community staff and learners) of the school. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what The school is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “The school” around your school. (skill: identify members of the (Head teacher, teachers, non-teaching 2. What is the importance school community staff and learners) of the school)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach The school to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify members of the (Head teacher, teachers, non-teaching 2. What is the importance school community staff and learners) of the school.
3. Make one local Kenya example of The school from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for The school: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 2 learner study The school?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what The school means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify members of the (Head teacher, teachers, non-teaching 2. What is the importance school community staff and learners) of the school.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
